float_frame.label: float-top side frames forward of the deck (x 2.1-4.9 m)

notes: Score = |trim| + 2|heel| (deg) + freeboard penalty below 0.15 m + 0.5 x (roll + pitch amplitude (deg) + deck accel (m/s2)) at the reference wave; edit the weights in exo01/optimise.py if your priorities differ.

Rear deck (x 0-2.1 m): the most forward row is the best for trim, but the COM stays aft of the float centroid - least trim -3.30 deg at x = 1.70 m. Asymmetric rows (port battery moved inboard) counter the heel from the port-side cabinet.

Float-top side frames (x 2.1-4.9 m, |y| 2.05 m, above the floats, outboard of the hull): least trim +0.15 deg at x = 3.62 m with rear-deck freeboard 0.36 m; the trim crosses zero at x = 3.54 m for the loads of this scenario. Whether the float cradle can carry 120 kg per battery is a structural question outside this model.
Trim sign: negative = rear deck down. Mass on the rear deck (people at the table) adds stern trim that the batteries can only partly compensate - re-run with the occupants you expect.
hydro_note: wave columns from the cached BEM of the base pose (exact COM transform; pose within tolerance)
